rationale: Multipart parsing previously returned maps missing file or fileName; it now rejects either missing part through non-null checks.
Concurrent permission calculation could overwrite permissions refreshed after parent-group lookup. Synchronizing calculation and reset preserves the refreshed permissions for subsequent searches.
Adapter request headers change from an application-only content type to JSON and gain Accept. The supplied files do not show how downstream differences affect this service's HTTP responses.
Two LDAP configuration constants are added without any changes that use them.

Namespaced target objects with omitted namespaces now have tracking metadata recomputed after namespace insertion. Previously only malformed cluster-scoped tracking was recomputed; comparison results can therefore differ.
Metadata cleanup reads batch-size configuration using the realm context. This changes cleanup batching without changing the metadata selected for deletion or a demonstrated HTTP result.
An empty configured server path is now normalized to slash. The supplied validator does not show whether consumers previously treated these paths differently for HTTP requests.

Advertised endpoint URLs now incorporate the configured prefix and optional callback address. Endpoint descriptors also support configured subprotocol information; previously URLs were resolved directly against the server URI.
Origins beginning with the HTTP loopback IP now receive CORS headers through the same unconditional branch as localhost origins. Previously they passed through the remaining origin checks.

Cancellation previously explicitly cancelled every descendant and caller. Callers with children are now reloaded after child cancellation so their aggregated status is retained instead of explicitly cancelled.
Password policy failures now return validation message objects rather than generic errors. The accepted password conditions remain the same but their error representation changes.
Unknown HTTP methods now mark the Jetty request handled after sending the method-not-allowed response. Previously this branch returned without preventing further unhandled-request processing.
The controller's empty-display-name rejection moves into a permission helper through a new argument. The helper implementation is absent so equivalent versus relaxed validation cannot be established.
Evaluation previously updated segmentID for every inspected segment. It now updates segmentID only when a variant is selected so unsuccessful evaluations no longer report the last inspected segment.
The controllers and response model change formatting and import placement while retaining the same request handling and response construction.
The path and build validation limits increase from 20 to 120 characters. Values between 21 and 120 characters can now pass validation.
Test router constructors and a test metrics manager are added. The production router constructors retain the same behavior.

User permission lookup now uses the MSAL home-account identifier instead of the prior unique identifier. Refresh also retains valid sessions when silent acquisition fails instead of propagating that failure.

WithTx and TxContext now reuse existing transactions rather than rejecting them. Existing AutoTx callers are renamed equivalently; the provided callers do not establish an HTTP request that previously encountered nesting rejection.
Only imports change in the session deletion handler. Its authorization checks and response-writing statements are unchanged.
Question pages using the short-ID permalink mode now omit the title suffix from their canonical URL. Previously only the ordinary ID permalink mode omitted that suffix.
The database scan report gains vulnerability counters. No supplied HTTP serializer or response mapping establishes whether these persistence fields are exposed to clients.
The wallet-response interface becomes a functional interface and parameter names change. Presentation lookup and response handling remain equivalent.

Stopping scan-all now records a stop marker checked while scheduling artifacts and cancels the iterator context. Previously only already-created execution tasks were stopped so scheduling could continue.

Startup failure of an optional web application no longer triggers the global unavailable-context shutdown check. Required contexts still fail startup so healthy HTTP contexts can remain available after optional-context failure.
An additional component-policy deprecation log call is added without changing policy enforcement or HTTP responses.
Process updates now prefill the request model from existing configuration before JSON binding. Omitted fields retain current values rather than receiving the previously initialized defaults.
Artifact operations switch file-manager methods and argument order. Implementations of those old and new methods are absent so a storage refactor cannot be distinguished from changed HTTP behavior.
The access DTO gains an adressesperreTilganger list component alongside its existing hierarchy and access map. Serialized DTO responses can now include this additional field.
Three package model classes are introduced without changes connecting them to an HTTP operation or replacing an existing response type.
Project-user fields gain documentation and read-only metadata tags. Their JSON names and the model's runtime handling code remain unchanged.
Project creation now trims names and rejects names shorter than the minimum after trimming. Project-name patches also trim stored names; previously surrounding whitespace was retained.
Trusted location updates move from a subtype into an ignored boolean flag. Client-deserialized locations remain untrusted and server-created trusted locations still update table or view state.
Negative page numbers and sizes previously failed assertions. They are now normalized to page one and size zero respectively; page zero also becomes page one.
The DNS lookup context gains a timeout cause. Lookup errors are still discarded and the same resolved addresses undergo the same private-range checks.
Diagnostics are retained in a field and passed into the transaction workspace manager. The shown catalog operations and diagnostic checks otherwise remain equivalent.
Kafka operations now use a bounded dedicated executor. When submission is rejected the handlers return a 503 overload error instead of submitting through the previous asynchronous executor.
Effective due dates replace due dates when constructing an Avro business-event payload. The supplied serializer does not change an HTTP response or API-visible stored loan data.

Attachment preview rendering now continues after cache-read failure and returns rendered bytes even when cache insertion fails. Previously preview retrieval delegated error handling to the cache remember operation.
The YAML API-version document model gains primarySpec. No supplied change connects this export-format field to a REST response or persisted API resource.
Batch checks previously emitted an empty error string when membership was unknown without an underlying error. In strict mode they now expose the recorded limitation in that field.
The settings-key enum replaces server.footer.links with server.sidebar.links. Its JSON creator now rejects the old key and recognizes the new key.

Missing compatibility rules now fall back to configured global defaults rather than always NONE. Setting NONE now stores an explicit rule instead of deleting the rule and potentially inheriting another level.
Submodel-element creation still delegates the same mutation. Only the Kafka creation event path is recomputed to include the child identifier or list index; no API-visible event consumer is supplied.
Protocol bindings gain a routingKey property with public accessors. Existing serialized operation bindings can therefore include an additional field.
Organization identity-provider links and domain lookups gain cached representations with delegation after updates. No changed authorization rule or response value is demonstrated.
Two-factor passkey responses now return immediately after the two-factor response handler. Previously the one-factor handler also ran and could overwrite the selected redirect response.
Request-path noise classification now recognizes root paths directly. Callers of this utility are absent so the files do not establish whether this affects responses or only logging.
Only comments and comment wrapping change in contract-test API stubs.
The existing protected-resource-metadata enablement checks move into a shared method. The middleware still checks the same two configuration locations in the same order.
The injected session repository type changes to its framework interface. Endpoint logic and repository method calls remain unchanged.

Startup password-hash configuration gains scrypt-variant validation and yescrypt constraints. The supplied configuration validators do not establish a changed HTTP operation or runtime hashing result.
A new audit-log persistence model and event-name list are added without an HTTP handler or code that populates and returns them.
Two persistence fetch-group definitions and their enum entries are removed. The component's serialized data properties and shown runtime behavior are unchanged.
The changed URL is constructed only inside an outgoing email notification. The supplied code does not return or store it through an HTTP API.

Explicit-timeseries recent-value queries now pass the requested office into the DAO. Previously that branch omitted office scope so identically named series from different offices could affect results.
Wallet responses may now submit a response JWT that is verified before processing. Previously only individual direct-post form fields were parsed into an authorization response.
Payment search logging redacts two values and the response-selection switch is rewritten equivalently. Request processing and HTTP response construction retain their behavior.
Comment-page requests now decode a short comment identifier before the service lookup. Previously the supplied identifier was passed through unchanged.

Entitlement mapping now tolerates missing purchase data and null contract lists. Previously these values could cause null dereferences; mapping now returns a null billing-provider identifier or an empty plan component.
Visitor callback signatures gain a context argument. No HTTP handler or callback implementation changes its output or stored state in the supplied changes.
Project update previously parsed a Project request body. It now requires name and office query parameters and performs a rename using the path's old name.

The patch removes conflicting pagination declarations and changes bean packages. The supplied before method mixes string parameters with numeric expressions so comparable running HTTP behavior cannot be established.
Repository interfaces gain a count method and a job-target repository type. No implementation or HTTP operation is changed to call them.

The after files contain unresolved merge-conflict markers around imports and fields. Although one branch adds environment details the supplied source does not define an executable HTTP implementation.
A new request-specific JARM JWKS GET route returns public ephemeral keys or state-dependent 400/404 responses. JARM key references now target this route instead of the general public JWKS endpoint.
Only deprecation documentation changes in the Kafka configuration model.
The Accept header remains readable from external requests but is no longer eligible for publication in external response headers. Previously both directions were enabled.
User-update permission checks move into another file with local variable renaming. The same field comparisons and permission decisions remain in place.
Failure to find a requested commit previously always produced an internal-server error. The handler now maps missing Git objects to not-found while retaining server errors for other failures.
Live and recorded video requests without channel now use channel one. Previously the unannotated primitive query parameter defaulted to zero.
HTTP bridge logging switches logging libraries and logger fields. Request handling and response-writing branches remain unchanged.

Expired sessions now attempt silent recovery. Failed renewals impose a one-minute retry delay where previously every near-expiry request retried; this can postpone a successful renewal and subsequent permission refresh.
Non-HTTPS return-URL rejection for live accounts now maps to 422 with a dedicated error code and field message. Previously this connector error followed the mapper's fallback error mapping.
Field-validation messages are now capitalized and receive a trailing period when absent. Previously their original capitalization and punctuation were returned.

Artifact-update helper methods become protected and explicitly require write authorization. Artifact and version creation also pass the authenticated principal as owner instead of leaving ownership to storage defaults.
Adding loan charges previously left disbursement charges unchanged. Fee charges are now accumulated and included when the disbursement period is converted to response data.
An explicit owner/admin/curator write check is replaced by checkCanWrite. The inherited helper implementation is absent so preservation or restriction of authorized callers cannot be determined.
Aggregate source information gains an annotationSourcesInfo list with public accessors and source-version detail objects. Serialized source-information responses can include the additional property.
Changes refactor and extend WireMock contract-test stubs. They do not change production HTTP handlers or persisted service data.

Imports previously returned 201 even for empty files or unsupported media types and after caught import exceptions. These cases now return 400 or 415 or 500 respectively; successful imports still return 201.
The changed throwable representation is used only as a validation log argument. Returned validation behavior is unchanged.
YAML document serialization omits empty metadata/name values and gains list/project document types. No supplied change exposes these import/export document models through an HTTP operation.
Removing the last workflow version now unpublishes a published workflow. Other removals refresh its public index; previously neither publication state nor index update occurred in this branch.
Modifier ordering and final local or parameter declarations change. Static-file lookup and connection-limiting behavior remain equivalent.
Access-log recording is added to success and error handling. The changes do not alter HTTP response bodies or statuses.
Only static-analysis suppression comments are added to check response construction.
Legacy plan security configuration now selects a named serialization mapper. The mapper implementation and target-property type are absent so the resulting HTTP value or type cannot be compared.
Connection validation now rejects invalid diversion identifiers and response types as well as self-diversion and topics on diversion targets. Previously these diversion-specific checks were absent.

Pattern annotations move from javax.validation to jakarta.validation without changing regexes. Framework version and validation registration are absent so changed enforcement versus equivalent namespace migration cannot be determined.

Endpoint uniqueness checks now invoke doCount with a transaction. The before file calls an absent two-argument overload and dependency wiring also changes so a comparable HTTP outcome cannot be established.
OAuth login and token-exchange trace events receive corrected subject/request context. HTTP processing and error response calls are unchanged.

Gitness gitspaces now use code_repo_ref instead of code_repo_url for repository resolution. Creation dereferences the new pointer and actions reject missing references so requests omitting this formerly absent field can fail.
Only the cache-library import changes to its version-two module path. Password validation conditions and cache usage in the supplied file remain unchanged.
A URI encoding test is added. No production HTTP implementation changes.
A business attribute-key constant is added without any code using it to change stored positions or responses.
New endpoint-tracking conversion helpers are defined without changes invoking them from API conversion or HTTP handlers.
A documentation spelling correction leaves lineage processing unchanged.
Supported saved commands are now explicitly ordered by description. Previously this query specified no ordering.
Git push and API reference/content operations no longer check merge-queue branch-update restrictions. Updates previously rejected solely by those restrictions can now proceed to the remaining checks.
Transaction execution interfaces and their endpoint-service call sites are renamed from executeWithResult to execute with the same transaction bodies.
Placeholder OAuth authorization and OIDC login responses change from 200/success to 405/failed. OAuth redirect is replaced by userinfo and a new OIDC redirect route.
More applications can use manifest revision updates instead of full generation. The supplied change broadens an optimization without demonstrating different manifests or API-visible results.

Implicit user subscriptions are now created even when a parent subscription already applies. Previously inheritance prevented the direct row so unsubscribing from the parent could remove the effective subscription.
Snapshot requests without an explicit limit now apply a positive configured default limit. Previously this branch left the result count unlimited.

Potential-entry recommended actions now receive the installation event's triggering user rather than the authenticated caller. Consequently actions can be associated with a different user or no known trigger user.

Routes switch to a ViewNameResolver in another package while the old implementation is removed. The replacement implementation is absent so theme fallback and rendered HTTP content cannot be compared.

A missing widget session registry is initialized to an empty default registry. Previously that case returned process uptime with zero session counts; no different statistic is established for the empty registry.
Only the database-library import switches to a fork. The supplied OAuth handler's queries and response handling are unchanged.
Timeout exceptions no longer satisfy the interruption utility. Its callers are not supplied so changes in HTTP status mapping or task handling cannot be established.
The change conditionally exposes administrative Prometheus metrics and adds supporting configuration. Payment API requests and responses are unaffected by this instrumentation.
Passkey imports now reject missing user handles and empty credential lists with bad-request errors. Previously these values reached credential storage without these checks.
Four grace fields are added to a Swagger-only response documentation class. No runtime loan response model or handler is changed.
An internal patch endpoint now injects an asynchronous-named service type. Neither service implementation is supplied so changes to completion timing or HTTP-visible failures cannot be established.
Missing products in review operations now produce 404 instead of 400. Handler priorities also change and malformed body or parameter exceptions are rethrown for framework handling.
The dry-run event endpoint loses its controller transaction annotation. The service implementation is absent so whether rollback or API-visible effects change cannot be established.

Group listing gains an optional subGroupsCount flag defaulting true. Counts can now be suppressed and subgroup counts are populated independently of brief representation where previously that branch depended on briefness.

Imported example responses gain supplied dispatch criteria. The updated callers and criteria values are absent so the files do not establish a changed mock HTTP response or API-visible imported value.

Bridge representations gain optional websocketConfiguration details. Creation/update conversion now persists enabled websocket settings and response conversion returns configured websocket path and subprotocol.

Consumer deletion now removes timestamp and endpoint entries through the close callback rather than immediately after handling deletion. Concurrent maps and snapshot iteration also prevent modification failures during consumer cleanup.
Variant annotations gain an errorMessage property with public accessors. Serialized annotation responses can now include the additional field.
Page-revision accessors move to equivalent generated accessors and constructors. A new audit-event enum is defined without code emitting those events.
Submodel mutations now share a lock. Concurrent creation and update requests can no longer interleave the guarded existence checks and mutations as before so duplicate or lost state can differ.

The internal Kafka message-key setting is renamed with deprecated accessors forwarding to the same value. The producer continues placing that value in the record key and no HTTP representation changes are shown.

Policy-condition values now require at least one character where empty values were previously allowed by this model. Expression conditions are also introduced with compilation and violation-type validation.
Certificate-attribute provider classes are added without changes invoking them from an HTTP processor or returning their attributes through an API.

Empty privilege-set collection operations gain standard empty-set semantics. The supplied files contain no authorization callers establishing whether these changed operations affect an HTTP permission decision.

The product-not-found message is computed equivalently and its identifier list is copied defensively. No supplied code mutates the original list after exception construction to change an HTTP response.

Deletion hooks now receive configured tracking annotations or labels through the shared tracker. Previously they always received an untruncated instance label so long names or annotation tracking could prevent successful hook handling.

Segment debug objects are allocated only when debug output is consumed and rollout uses a preformatted flag-ID string. The shown response inclusion and evaluation inputs retain the same intended values.
Location-level listings gain an include-aliases option defaulting false. When requested the DAO can supply aliases and nonempty alias lists are serialized as an additional response field.
Configuration reload gains an informational log statement without changing reload processing or HTTP output.
Vision models gain an optional Run field and scheduling helpers. The files do not show an HTTP operation returning the model or invoking the new scheduling behavior.
Variant annotations gain a genomicLocationExplanation property with public accessors. Serialized annotation responses can now include the additional field.
A new helper can populate deduplicated vulnerability aliases but no supplied change invokes it. Existing finding construction and response population remain unchanged.
Schema duplicate-ID checking no longer pre-reserves the initial-column-ID constant. A field using that ID is now accepted unless another field actually duplicates it.
